chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

We both asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the al-mamouma fracture, so he said: 'Regarding it is a third of the wergild, and regarding the al-jaifa is a third of the wergild, and regarding the al-mudhiha is five camels.'

key_terms.الشَّجَّةِ الْمَأْمُومَةِ: A fracture of the head reaching the brain
key_terms.الْجَائِفَةِ: A fracture that penetrates deeply into the brain
key_terms.الْمُوضِحَةِ: A fracture that exposes the bone
key_terms.خَمْسٌ مِنَ الْإِبِلِ: Five camels, a specific unit of compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money compensation for specific head fractures in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through prominent chains in al-Kafi, details the specific blood money (diyah) for three distinct types of head injuries: al-mamouma (superficial), al-jaifa (penetrating), and al-mudhiha (deep enough to reach the brain). It assigns a third of the full diyah to the first two and five camels to the third, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precise anatomical classification to determine compensation severity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Zayd Al Shahham who both said,

‘We both asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Al-Mamouma fracture (the head fracture reaching the brain). So heasws said: ‘Regarding it is a third of the wergild, and regarding Al-Jaifa (skull injury reaching the inside of the brain) is a third of the wergild, and regarding Al-Mowziha (bone exposing injury) is five from the camels’.
